title: The Diesel Midterms
description_html:
Energy prices are up — and President Trump is out of time to bring them down before the US midterm elections. 

On today’s Big Take podcast, David Gura breaks down the factors keeping prices high and how much it could cost the Republican party with White House reporter Josh Wingrove and Will Kubzansky, who covers gasoline, diesel and jet fuel. 

We have a special Bloomberg subscription offer for podcast listeners at Bloomberg.com/podcastoffer.

Host: David Gura; Guests: Josh Wingrove and Will Kubzansky; Produced by Julia Press, David Fox, Julia Weaver; Edited by Naomi Shavin; Engineering by Sean Carter.

News.
How much nuance is the president, is the White House using in talking about the drivers of these higher energy prices?
Well, off camera, they will make some of the same arguments.
You know, inflation adjusted, it's not as bad as it used to be. $100 oil isn't $100 oil the way we used to think about it.
But in reality, it's a five alarm political fire for them.

And it is not only seemed to have put the House further and further out of reach in these midterm elections, but expanded the Senate map into fairly jaw-dropping places like Kansas and South Carolina, where the president is campaigning.
Gas prices are very closely correlated to the president's approval rating.
And so you've seen Trump go around, kind of knock on every door, open every cupboard, try to find every gallon of gasoline and diesel he can find anywhere, including from Vladimir Putin.
I'm David Gurra, and this is The Big Take from Bloomberg News.
Today on the show, energy prices are up.
Will they take down Trump's party in the midterms?
I'm going to start by having you both introduce yourselves, first name, last name, and what you do here at Bloomberg.
Josh, let me start with you.
I'm Josh Wingrove.
I'm a White House reporter here at Bloomberg.
My name is Will Kubzanski.
I cover refined products for Bloomberg.
So that's fuels like gasoline, diesel, jet fuel.
This is a classic Bloomberg beat.
Very niche. It is so Bloomberg, yeah.
Will, before I sat down, I checked Brent Crude.
It's at $106.50 a barrel, thereabouts.
In the U.S., the average price of a gallon of gasoline, according to.
AAA, $4.33 a gallon.
Diesel's about $6.
Put all of this in context for us.
How high are energy prices right now?
They're high.
Energy prices... at least on fuels, are at the highest point for this time of year that we've ever seen. $6 diesel was something that was unprecedented until this year alone.
To be fair, right, you can go back and you can do inflation adjustments and you can say, well, in 2008 and in 2022, maybe it was more comparable.
But in terms of the absolute number drivers are seeing at the pump, it has never been higher for diesel.
And this time of year, it's never been higher for gasoline.
How much of this is directly.
Attributable to the war in the Middle East, the war with Iran?
This is a question that we have spent a while trying to sort of get a solid answer on.
The White House has said Russia is to blame for diesel prices.
Look, if you go back to the chart of Brent crude and you go to, you know, February 27th and then, you know, first week of March when the war began, the cost of oil spiked.
And that was certainly the cause of higher gas prices, higher diesel prices in the first months of the war.
The amount of supplies that we lost coming from the Middle East through the Strait of Hormuz is much larger than the amount of supply that we lost from Russia.
With that said, as Ukraine has picked up its drone strikes on Russian refineries, the barrels we have lost from over there have risen, and that has also contributed to rising prices.
Will, we got this reading of the Consumer Price Index, the latest read of that index this morning.

Gasoline prices, that index up 9% in September, made up over half the monthly increase for all items. situate energy in kind of the broader U.S. economy, the degree to which these rising prices are affecting the overall economy?
I mean, look, gasoline and diesel, I think, are actually two really good ways to look at the economy because gasoline is, you know, a personal consumption item.
You're a driver, you know, you live in Michigan or Wisconsin or Iowa and you see the price every day.
You're feeling that pain every day.
You're feeling it every day and you fill up your car and you say, I'm going to put X amount of money into the tank.
With that said, comparatively, if you think about your expenditures as a broad picture, there's obviously a lot more than just gasoline.
Diesel prices seep through into everything else.
Diesel is a fuel that is primarily used for, aside from agriculture and industry, it's used for trucking.
The workhorse fuel.
Workhorse fuel of the global economy.
We've said that a lot.
Diesel prices... push inflation higher.
We might not be seeing the impacts of higher diesel prices right now in the inflation print because it takes time.
There's pass-through from agriculture to truckers to grocery stores, but it's sort of a squeeze on both ends that is making the economy really feel this.
Josh, you've spent a lot of time with the president recent weeks.
You've been on the campaign trail with him as he's been stumping for Republican candidates.
How much is this in energy prices How much has it turned into that?
I think it is very substantially that under a broader umbrella, this is a cost election.
This is an affordability election like the last two were.
We're seeing that in particular in a lot of polling that shows certain demographic groups.
Latino voters, for instance, swung to President Trump substantially in 2024 over concerns about prices.
They're now swinging back in such a jarring way that some of the gerrymanders that Trump did to try to cling to the House majority are maybe even backfiring.
And so I think for Trump, The question is, you know, what can you do to calm voter concerns on that?
We've seen him do things like announce checks, both $90 checks to certain people, as well as the promise of a $5, 000 check that not a lot of people think is ever, of course, real.
But he's trying to respond to it in some ways.
But then he's also Donald Trump, and he can't kind of help himself, but like veer off into other topics, including renovations and this and that.
And so there's not been a consistent message from the administration on what they're doing on this.
And that's, you know, where it's sort of landed.
Now, Trump's administration right now is sort of holding out hope that things won't be bad.
Republicans still have a lot of money.
It's possible that they can sort of thread the needle, you know, treat the Senate in particular as sort of a last ditch effort.
One official telling our colleague, Catherine Lucy, it's now sort of a firewall.
But the polls on that don't look good either, because if states like Texas and Iowa and Ohio and Alaska are going to flip, or at risk of flipping, that really changes the math.
This wasn't supposed to be a very good cycle for Democrats, but if, you know, that they even have a hope of flipping the Senate at all is an indication of how bad things have gotten for Republicans.
We're like two weeks out, Will.
I'm not going to make you opine on the politics, but let me just ask you about the time horizon here.
Is there any hope or likelihood that in that period we could see these prices of gas, of diesel, of oil come down at all substantially?
It's a good question.
I mean, there is sort of an upper bound on how much prices can move within two, three weeks before election day.
You know, the dynamic everyone always talks about with gas prices is rockets and feathers, which is when crude oil goes up, prices for gas go skyrocketing up right with it.
And then feathers, when it comes down, it sort of trickles down slowly.
Right now, what we're seeing in sort of the gasoline and diesel futures markets doesn't really seem to indicate that we're getting a massive price relief anytime soon.
The other thing that's going on right now is right now the U.S. has seasonally really low stockpiles of both gasoline and diesel compared to sort of normal fall months.

So that means that whenever there's a refinery that has an issue, if there is a pipeline that has a problem, if there's a storm that means you can't ship fuel from, say, the Gulf Coast to the Northeast, that is going to meaningfully impact the price of fuel.
So yeah, two, three-week horizon, you could certainly see prices decrease, but not by blockbuster margins.
Josh, I was going to ask you what levers the president has to pull and indeed has pulled in recent weeks.
I'll take your cupboard metaphor, though, as he's kind of rooting through that cupboard.
What has he found?
Well, the Europeans agreed to release some stockpiles, although I think there are questions about how much and how quickly that will come.
The most controversial deal, of course, is the deal with Russia to release diesel.
The administration has not really been clear on what that means.
There's a bipartisan group of senators who've objected to that, saying it's against the law.

There's a 2022 law banning direct Russian energy sales into the U.S. The administration has seemed to signal that it won't come to the U.S. and instead would hit the global market and then, you know, maybe bring prices down generally, including here in the U.S., but that will only expand the criticism that Trump is giving a lifeline to Putin.
You know, why are you doing this if it's not even directly coming to the U.S. in the first place?
I mean, you know, this has come up in other calls, including over the weekend with the Canadian prime minister, according to Carney's office.
They discussed diesel as well.
So it seems like he's Basically mentioning it in every call, calling anyone he can to try to shake loose what he can.
And this is part of a pattern of him, you know, not being afraid to use the administration and its policies to an electoral end in a pretty aggressive way.
I think right now he's just kind of running out of cupboard doors.
Time is running out.

And their question is, can they reallocate money fast enough in particular to keep states like Kansas not affected? a swing state when it comes to the Senate, although they do have a Democratic governor, from flipping.

And if they can do that, if they can sort of cling on to maybe like a 51-49 or a 50-50 Senate with J.D. Vance breaking the ties, then, you know, they think that maybe that's a better case scenario than the alternatives that are in front of them at the moment.
Will, I'm going to ask you to level set here.
So the president announces this diesel deal.
Russia's going to supply the global market with around 36 million barrels of diesel.
What's the impact of that likely to be if, in fact, it does happen?
The short version is, at least in the short term, pretty limited.
Analysts are pretty underwhelmed by the amount of diesel that Trump announced and then that Russia later confirmed.
And I should just say these numbers are moving targets.
We're sort of getting changing numbers from the Russians on how much they're going to release.
We don't know when those ships are going to load.
There are legitimate legal hurdles to getting those cargoes to the U.S., as we discussed.
But the initial shipments, especially pre-election, are not going to be anywhere close to large enough to move the price of diesel.
Look, 36 million barrels at the margin, and this is sort of over. multiple months, and we're talking about maybe a resumption of monthly exports sort of into the winter.
Anything helps. The diesel market is incredibly undersupplied right now.
Any additional barrel is helpful to a farmer in Brazil or someone looking to heat their home in Europe.
With that said, Compared to where Russia was, Russia is normally the world's second largest exporter of diesel.
This still leaves the market pretty short.
I would actually say really quite short of where it needs to be to sort of resolve those supply issues that it's facing right now.
Coming up, more of my conversation with Josh Wingrove and Will Kosansky.
Josh, a busy weekend.

So we had this announcement about diesel exports from the president, announced that the Treasury Department was issuing a waiver to Russia to be able to do this, ending sanctions that had been in place effectively.
And then he announced this so-called energy truce between Ukraine and Russia.
What has that meant, if anything, in actual fact, over the last few days?
I mean, he has said that it is a truce that exists because he declared it to exist.
And so, by extension, he's admitting that they didn't agree to it. or at least both countries haven't.

It is tenuous at best, and it is not only sort of fueling questions about the president's lifeline or olive branch to Russia, but renewing all these questions about what, if anything, the U.S. will do to support Ukraine to sort of drive the circumstances to force some kind of a ceasefire or truce between Russia and Ukraine.
Europeans They don't like this.
They think that it is a hurting and undercutting efforts to reach a deal of some kind and to support Ukraine.
Because, of course, the question is, well, if Putin gets all this revenue from oil. and from diesel and just keeps hammering along in the war.
And Trump tries to clip the wings of Zelensky to fire back and use drone strikes or whatever to limit Russian energy production.
Then that tilts a pretty, what already is a pretty precarious sort of balance a little bit towards Russia or perhaps more than a little bit.
So there's like the questionable or dubious legality of this.
There's the blowback that the president has gotten from his peers, many leaders in Europe pushing back on this.
And then there's domestic pushback as well, Josh.
And I wanted to ask you about that and sort of what it says about the political moment that we're in, that you have lawmakers speaking out against the president for doing this.
You have legislation in the name of Ronald Reagan pushing back on this as well.
What does that tell you about the president's ability to consolidate power in this very immediate run up to the midterms?
Yeah. And also this seems to fly in the face of the Lindsey Graham Russia sanctions bill that was, you know, passed not that long ago.

We are starting to see Republicans more comfortable speaking out against the president in some cases because they have to, because they're seeking reelection in either swing districts or what they hoped weren't swing districts, but suddenly are because the tide has come out 10 points.

Or they just are trying to send public warnings to the president and they're fearful that he's getting poor advice from his inner circle. which has remained sort of unchanged but shrinking since he took office again for the second time in 2025.
And so I think sort of overall, you kind of sense among Republicans certainly that they expect to lose the House and that now, you know, this sort of despondency that the Senate might flip.
Will, as you know so well covering this, and as the president I think is learning, there's an intractability to the global energy market.
And we've seen this string of attacks everywhere.
It's taken place in Saudi Arabia.
The Houthis have attacked the airport in Riyadh, Aramco.
Facilities as well.
What effect is that having on prices globally?
Yeah, any additional conflict in the Middle East adds to what is called the risk premium for oil.
Any expectation of increased fighting, of pipelines being attacked, of increased attacks on shipping adds to the price of oil.
And the price of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz right now has gone up.
There's still a lot of oil that's making its way out. but the risk of attacks from Iranians has risen.
And so that's risen the price of freight.
And in turn, the price of freight all around the world is going up.
So it's this sort of chain reaction that's pulling different parts of the string and you're seeing the price react in turn.
Josh, how is that shaping the president's calculus when it comes to the Middle East?
I mean, it's really been kind of a back and forth.
Would he get involved again in the Middle East or not?
Yes, he will.
No, he won't.
Maybe he'll wait to the midterms.
Kind of classic Trump uncertainty or projected uncertainty about that when it comes to these attacks that we've seen in Saudi Arabia.
He has floated the idea that he might be willing to support Saudi Arabia in going after the Houthis.
Where does that stand?
What's your sense of his thinking when it comes to further engagement or additional engagement in the Middle East?

I talked to a White House official yesterday and asked them, hey, is this on the table, both the question of helping the Saudis with targeting information, for instance, or actually more broadly joining the war with U.S. strikes in particular? they really didn't want to bite on that.
The source indicated that it really wasn't top of mind.

I think the broader concern is the president would see this as a risk of looking like he's getting further into a foreign entanglement at a time when there's a lot of concerns in his base about this already.
He's, of course, declared victory several times over the course of this conflict with Iran.
And so right now, the signals that they're sending are not a no, But very, very cool interest about getting dragged further and further into this.
And of course, there's good reason with that, right?
Trump has reshaped the Republican Party in part with a sort of message of not getting involved in these foreign wars.
And I think it just remains one of the thornier forks in the road facing them about whether they decide to double down and get further involved.

Into this, we might see that potentially after the election or if they just leave it to the Saudis to try to deal with it and, of course, risk the Saudis getting frustrated that the U.S. isn't there to help them deal with the collateral fallout of all of this.
Josh, I'm going to pick up on something you said there, which is what happens after the midterm elections.
How are you thinking about that?
You know, if control of Congress changes, for instance...
Do we have a president who is as engaged with this issue of energy prices, more engaged, less engaged?
How do you think about that going forward?
In the past, a sort of cornered Trump has been a more unpredictable Trump.
And so I think it's really difficult to know.
He's, of course, teed up the prospect of reengaging with strikes on Iran after the election.
He's sort of spoken on both sides of his mouth on that.
So I think sort of basically anything happens. is on the table.
But the dynamic is going to shift here in Washington.

At minimum, if the House flips, Trump's going to be facing a range of investigations from the Oversight Committee, among other committees about, you know, family business and any conduct of the administration.
I mean, the list will go on and on and on and on.
And all that will be playing out in the context of the 2028 race ramping up, his own vice president being increasingly ensnared by these questions.
And so I think the domestic politics are going to get messy pretty quick for him.
As we see it here, Trump's first goal is get to the midterms with the best outcome possible.
After that, I think a lot of things are on the table, but he will be increasingly confined to executive power and not congressional power.
And that could manifest sort of either way.
Either he's focused more domestically and dealing with whatever's going on politically, or he decides that this is a legacy issue and he wants to engage in it.
No one knows which way he's going to go.
This is The Big Take from Bloomberg News.
I'm David Gurra.
To get more from The Big Take and unlimited access to all of Bloomberg.com, subscribe today at Bloomberg.com slash podcast offer.
Thanks for listening.
We'll be back tomorrow.

The diesel market is incredibly undersupplied right now. Any additional barrel is helpful to a farmer in Brazil or someone looking to heat their home in Europe.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: With that said, Compared to where Russia was, Russia is normally the world's second largest exporter of diesel. This still leaves the market pretty short. I would actually say really quite short of where it needs to be to sort of resolve those supply issues that it's facing right now.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Coming up, more of my conversation with Josh Wingrove and Will Kosansky. Josh, a busy weekend. So we had this announcement about diesel exports from the president, announced that the Treasury Department was issuing a waiver to Russia to be able to do this, ending sanctions that had been in place effectively. And then he announced this so-called energy truce between Ukraine and Russia. What has that meant, if anything, in actual fact, over the last few days?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: I mean, he has said that it is a truce that exists because he declared it to exist. And so, by extension, he's admitting that they didn't agree to it. or at least both countries haven't. It is tenuous at best, and it is not only sort of fueling questions about the president's lifeline or olive branch to Russia, but renewing all these questions about what, if anything, the U.S. will do to support Ukraine to sort of drive the circumstances to force some kind of a ceasefire or truce between Russia and Ukraine.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Europeans They don't like this. They think that it is a hurting and undercutting efforts to reach a deal of some kind and to support Ukraine. Because, of course, the question is, well, if Putin gets all this revenue from oil. and from diesel and just keeps hammering along in the war. And Trump tries to clip the wings of Zelensky to fire back and use drone strikes or whatever to limit Russian energy production.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Then that tilts a pretty, what already is a pretty precarious sort of balance a little bit towards Russia or perhaps more than a little bit.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: So there's like the questionable or dubious legality of this. There's the blowback that the president has gotten from his peers, many leaders in Europe pushing back on this. And then there's domestic pushback as well, Josh. And I wanted to ask you about that and sort of what it says about the political moment that we're in, that you have lawmakers speaking out against the president for doing this.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: You have legislation in the name of Ronald Reagan pushing back on this as well. What does that tell you about the president's ability to consolidate power in this very immediate run up to the midterms?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Yeah. And also this seems to fly in the face of the Lindsey Graham Russia sanctions bill that was, you know, passed not that long ago. We are starting to see Republicans more comfortable speaking out against the president in some cases because they have to, because they're seeking reelection in either swing districts or what they hoped weren't swing districts, but suddenly are because the tide has come out 10 points.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Or they just are trying to send public warnings to the president and they're fearful that he's getting poor advice from his inner circle. which has remained sort of unchanged but shrinking since he took office again for the second time in 2025. And so I think sort of overall, you kind of sense among Republicans certainly that they expect to lose the House and that now, you know, this sort of despondency that the Senate might flip.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Will, as you know so well covering this, and as the president I think is learning, there's an intractability to the global energy market. And we've seen this string of attacks everywhere. It's taken place in Saudi Arabia. The Houthis have attacked the airport in Riyadh, Aramco.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Facilities as well. What effect is that having on prices globally?

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Yeah, any additional conflict in the Middle East adds to what is called the risk premium for oil. Any expectation of increased fighting, of pipelines being attacked, of increased attacks on shipping adds to the price of oil. And the price of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz right now has gone up. There's still a lot of oil that's making its way out. but the risk of attacks from Iranians has risen.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: And so that's risen the price of freight. And in turn, the price of freight all around the world is going up. So it's this sort of chain reaction that's pulling different parts of the string and you're seeing the price react in turn.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Josh, how is that shaping the president's calculus when it comes to the Middle East? I mean, it's really been kind of a back and forth. Would he get involved again in the Middle East or not?

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Yes, he will. No, he won't. Maybe he'll wait to the midterms.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Kind of classic Trump uncertainty or projected uncertainty about that when it comes to these attacks that we've seen in Saudi Arabia. He has floated the idea that he might be willing to support Saudi Arabia in going after the Houthis.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Where does that stand?

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: What's your sense of his thinking when it comes to further engagement or additional engagement in the Middle East?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: I talked to a White House official yesterday and asked them, hey, is this on the table, both the question of helping the Saudis with targeting information, for instance, or actually more broadly joining the war with U.S. strikes in particular? they really didn't want to bite on that. The source indicated that it really wasn't top of mind. I think the broader concern is the president would see this as a risk of looking like he's getting further into a foreign entanglement at a time when there's a lot of concerns in his base about this already.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: He's, of course, declared victory several times over the course of this conflict with Iran. And so right now, the signals that they're sending are not a no, But very, very cool interest about getting dragged further and further into this. And of course, there's good reason with that, right? Trump has reshaped the Republican Party in part with a sort of message of not getting involved in these foreign wars.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And I think it just remains one of the thornier forks in the road facing them about whether they decide to double down and get further involved. Into this, we might see that potentially after the election or if they just leave it to the Saudis to try to deal with it and, of course, risk the Saudis getting frustrated that the U.S. isn't there to help them deal with the collateral fallout of all of this.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Josh, I'm going to pick up on something you said there, which is what happens after the midterm elections. How are you thinking about that? You know, if control of Congress changes, for instance... Do we have a president who is as engaged with this issue of energy prices, more engaged, less engaged?

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: How do you think about that going forward?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: In the past, a sort of cornered Trump has been a more unpredictable Trump. And so I think it's really difficult to know. He's, of course, teed up the prospect of reengaging with strikes on Iran after the election. He's sort of spoken on both sides of his mouth on that. So I think sort of basically anything happens. is on the table. But the dynamic is going to shift here in Washington.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: At minimum, if the House flips, Trump's going to be facing a range of investigations from the Oversight Committee, among other committees about, you know, family business and any conduct of the administration. I mean, the list will go on and on and on and on. And all that will be playing out in the context of the 2028 race ramping up, his own vice president being increasingly ensnared by these questions.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And so I think the domestic politics are going to get messy pretty quick for him. As we see it here, Trump's first goal is get to the midterms with the best outcome possible. After that, I think a lot of things are on the table, but he will be increasingly confined to executive power and not congressional power. And that could manifest sort of either way. Either he's focused more domestically and dealing with whatever's going on politically, or he decides that this is a legacy issue and he wants to engage in it.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: No one knows which way he's going to go.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: This is The Big Take from Bloomberg News. I'm David Gurra.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: To get more from The Big Take and unlimited access to all of Bloomberg.com, subscribe today at Bloomberg.com slash podcast offer.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Thanks for listening. We'll be back tomorrow.

study.one_liner_ko: 유가와 디젤 가격이 치솟으면서 트럼프가 중간선거 전에 가격을 잡을 수단을 거의 다 써버렸고, 공화당이 상원까지 위협받고 있다는 분석이다.
summary_ko: 브렌트유는 배럴당 약 106달러, 미국 휘발유는 갤런당 4.33달러, 디젤은 약 6.30달러다. 디젤은 사상 최고, 휘발유는 이맘때 기준 사상 최고다.
가격 급등의 주원인은 이란 전쟁 이후 호르무즈 해협 공급 차질이다. 우크라이나의 러시아 정유시설 드론 공격도 부분적으로 가격을 밀어올렸다.
디젤은 트럭 운송을 통해 농업, 식료품 등 모든 곳으로 전가되는 '일꾼 연료'다. 그 영향이 물가 지표에 나타나기까지는 시차가 있다.
백악관 기자 Josh는 이번 선거가 '생활비 선거'라고 본다. 트럼프는 수표 지급 약속, 유럽의 비축유 방출, 러시아산 디젤 거래 등 온갖 방법을 동원하지만 일관된 메시지가 없다.
러시아 디젤 3,600만 배럴 거래는 단기 효과가 제한적이고 법적 논란도 크다. 유럽과 공화당 상원의원들도 반발한다. 중동 추가 분쟁은 위험 프리미엄과 운임을 더 올린다.
선거 이후에는 하원을 뺏길 경우 조사와 2028 대선 경쟁으로 정치 상황이 복잡해지고, 트럼프의 중동 개입 여부도 불확실하다.
study.summary_en: So this Big Take episode is about the diesel midterms. Basically, fuel prices are at record highs for this time of year, mostly because of the Iran war and the disruption around the Strait of Hormuz, with Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian refineries adding to it. Diesel matters because it feeds into everything, from trucking to groceries. Trump is trying every lever he can, from stockpile releases to a controversial Russian diesel deal, but analysts say the impact is limited before election day. And politically, Republicans are worried about losing the House and maybe even the Senate. After November, nobody really knows whether he'll double down in the Middle East or turn inward.

expressions.quote: it's a five alarm political fire for them
expressions.nuance_ko: 불이 크게 났을 때 소방서가 울리는 5단계 경보에서 나온 말. 정치, 사업 위기를 극적으로 표현할 때 쓴다. 'a five-alarm fire' 뒤에 분야를 붙여 변형해도 된다.
examples: The server outage during the product launch was a five-alarm fire for the whole team.
When the biggest client threatened to leave, it turned into a five-alarm fire overnight.
Honestly, the airline strike is a five-alarm fire for anyone traveling this week.

similar.example: It's a full-blown crisis now, not just a hiccup.
We need all hands on deck to fix this before Monday.

expressions.quote: they can sort of thread the needle
expressions.meaning_ko: 좁은 길을 아슬아슬하게 통과하다, 어려운 균형을 맞추다
expressions.nuance_ko: 양쪽의 제약을 모두 만족시켜야 하는 어려운 상황에서 성공적으로 길을 찾는다는 뜻. 협상, 정책, 일정 등에 두루 쓴다. 'sort of' 같은 완화 표현과 자주 붙는다.
examples: We have to thread the needle between cutting costs and not losing our best people.
She managed to thread the needle in the meeting and keep both sides happy.
Driving through that narrow alley, he really threaded the needle.

similar.example: Managers walk a tightrope between honesty and morale.
We're trying to strike a balance between speed and quality.

expressions.quote: gas prices is rockets and feathers
expressions.meaning_ko: 오를 땐 로켓처럼, 내릴 땐 깃털처럼 천천히 (가격의 비대칭 반응)
expressions.nuance_ko: 원자재 가격이 오르면 소비자 가격은 즉각 오르고, 내릴 땐 느리게 내리는 현상을 가리키는 경제 용어. 휘발유뿐 아니라 임대료, 대출금리 등에도 비유적으로 쓴다.
examples: Grocery prices follow the rockets-and-feathers pattern: they shoot up fast and come down slowly.
Mortgage rates seem to be rockets and feathers lately.
Everyone complains about rockets and feathers, but few stores actually cut prices quickly.

similar.example: Prices are sticky on the way down.
There's asymmetric pass-through from wholesale to retail.

expressions.quote: to try to cling to the House majority
expressions.nuance_ko: 권력, 희망, 우위 등을 놓치기 직전에 간신히 붙잡는 느낌이 있다. 약간 부정적, 절박한 뉘앙스. 'cling on to'로도 쓴다.
examples: The team is clinging to a one-point lead with two minutes left.
Some managers cling to old processes even when they obviously don't work.
He clung to the hope that the flight would still leave on time.

similar.example: We're holding on to our market share for now.
The deal is hanging on by a thread.

expressions.quote: this seems to fly in the face of the Lindsey Graham Russia sanctions bill
expressions.meaning_ko: ~에 정면으로 반하다, 상식, 규칙, 증거와 어긋나다
expressions.nuance_ko: 행동이나 결정이 기존 규칙, 상식, 약속과 노골적으로 충돌할 때 쓴다. 비판적인 톤이므로 의견을 말할 때 'seems to'로 완화하면 좋다.
examples: Raising prices again flies in the face of everything we told customers.
That decision flies in the face of common sense.
Her claim flies in the face of the data we saw last quarter.

similar.example: This plan runs counter to our earlier commitments.
His view goes against the grain of the group.

expressions.quote: he can't kind of help himself, but like veer off into other topics
expressions.meaning_ko: 자제하지 못하다, 어쩔 수 없이 ~하고 만다
expressions.nuance_ko: 'can't help himself, but (he) ~' 구조로 습관적 충동을 약간 놀리듯 말할 때 쓴다. 뒤의 'veer off into (topics)'는 '화제가 딴 데로 새다'라는 유용한 연어다.
examples: He can't help himself; every meeting turns into a lecture.
I know I should stay on topic, but I can't help myself when we talk about travel.
My boss can't help himself, he always veers off into football.

similar.example: Sorry, I went off on a tangent there.
I can't resist a good bargain.

expressions.quote: they really didn't want to bite on that
expressions.meaning_ko: (질문, 미끼에) 응하다, 반응하다. 부정형은 답변을 피하다
expressions.nuance_ko: 기자의 질문이나 도발에 넘어가 입장을 밝히는 것을 'bite'라고 한다. 'didn't want to bite'는 '말을 아꼈다, 답을 피했다'는 뜻. 뉴스 인터뷰나 협상에서 자주 쓴다.
examples: I asked her about the merger rumors, but she wouldn't bite.
The CEO didn't bite on the reporter's question about layoffs.
I tried to start an argument about politics, but nobody bit.

similar.example: I didn't take the bait and kept my tone calm.
The spokesperson declined to comment.

expressions.quote: I'm going to ask you to level set here
expressions.meaning_ko: 기본 사실과 기준을 먼저 정리하다, 눈높이를 맞추다
expressions.nuance_ko: 논의를 깊이 들어가기 전에 모두가 같은 이해를 하도록 배경, 숫자를 짚는 것. 비즈니스 회의에서 많이 쓰는 표현이다. 'Let's level set' 형태로 회의를 시작할 때 유용하다.
examples: Before we dive in, let me level set on where we are on the budget.
Can you level set for those who missed last week's meeting?
I'd like to level set expectations about the timeline.

similar.expression: get everyone on the same page
similar.example: Let's get everyone on the same page first.
Let me set the stage with a few numbers.

expressions.quote: to try to shake loose what he can
expressions.nuance_ko: 단단히 붙어 있는 것(정보, 자원, 승인)을 힘을 줘서 풀어내는 느낌. 'shake loose some funding/information'처럼 쓴다. 약간 구어적이고 끈질긴 노력의 뉘앙스가 있다.
examples: I'm trying to shake loose a few more days from the vendor.
The reporter finally shook loose some details from the source.
We called every supplier to shake loose any spare stock.

similar.example: I couldn't pry out the answer from him.
We squeezed out a few extra hours.

expressions.quote: teed up the prospect of reengaging with strikes on Iran
expressions.meaning_ko: (다음 단계를 위해) 준비해 두다, 가능성을 띄우다
expressions.nuance_ko: 골프에서 공을 티에 올려놓는 데서 온 말. 앞으로의 행동이나 논의를 위해 판을 깔아놓는다는 뜻. 'tee up a discussion/decision/announcement'로 회의에서 자주 쓴다.
examples: I'll tee up the conversation with the client before you join.
The earlier report teed up the big announcement nicely.
She teed up a question that everyone had been avoiding.

similar.example: We laid the groundwork for the deal months ago.
He floated the idea of a four-day week.

expressions.quote: whether they decide to double down and get further involved
expressions.nuance_ko: 이미 택한 입장이나 투자를 비판에도 불구하고 오히려 강화한다는 뜻. 중립적으로도 쓰지만 고집이라는 뉘앙스를 띠기도 한다. 'double down on'으로 대상을 붙인다.
examples: After the criticism, the company doubled down on its new pricing.
Instead of backing off, he doubled down on his argument.
We should double down on what's working and cut the rest.

similar.example: She dug in her heels during the negotiation.
Let's stay the course for another quarter.

expressions.quote: as he's been stumping for Republican candidates
expressions.meaning_ko: ~를 위해 유세하다, 지지 연설을 하러 다니다
expressions.nuance_ko: 선거 캠페인에서 후보를 위해 지역을 돌며 지지를 호소하는 것. 'on the campaign trail'과 같이 뉴스에서 자주 나온다. 비정치 맥락에서는 '열심히 홍보하다'로 가볍게 쓸 수도 있다.
examples: The governor is stumping for her party's candidates across the state.
My friend has been stumping for that new restaurant to everyone he meets.
Former leaders often stump for allies before elections.

similar.example: She hit the campaign trail in March.
We need to drum up support for the proposal.

vocab.example: The ceasefire is tenuous at best, so I wouldn't count on it.
His job situation feels precarious after the restructuring.
People underestimate the intractability of housing costs in big cities.
There was a mood of despondency in the office after the results came out.
She got ensnared in a legal dispute she never wanted.
The jump from quiet countryside to the city was jarring.
Honestly, I was underwhelmed by the product demo.
The pass-through from higher shipping costs to store prices takes a few months.

warmup.q: How have rising fuel or grocery prices affected your daily life recently?
warmup.hint_ko: 통근, 장보기, 여행 등 구체적 변화와 소비 습관의 조정을 이야기해 본다.

warmup.q: Which prices do you notice most often, and why do some prices stick in your mind more than others?
warmup.hint_ko: 휘발유처럼 매일 보는 가격 vs 가끔 사는 것. 빈도와 체감 물가의 관계.

opinion.q: Do you think voters should hold leaders responsible for prices that are largely driven by global events?
opinion.hint_ko: 정부의 실제 통제력, 유권자의 체감, 책임 소재와 정치적 현실 사이의 간극을 논의.

opinion.q: What makes a message from a leader consistent or confusing during a crisis?
opinion.hint_ko: 일관된 메시지의 요건(단순함, 반복), 화제 이탈의 위험, 신뢰에 미치는 영향.

debate.q: Should governments release strategic reserves or make controversial deals to bring fuel prices down before an election?
debate.for: Households are hurting now, and even small relief matters. Using every available tool is a government's job, and diplomacy is always messy.
debate.against: It looks like electoral manipulation, short-term fixes barely move prices, and controversial deals can undermine allies and the rule of law.

roleplay.scenario: You and a colleague are preparing a briefing for your leadership team on how rising fuel costs are hitting your company's logistics budget ahead of a big seasonal peak.
roleplay.your_role: Operations lead who has to level set the facts and propose a plan.
roleplay.partner_role: Skeptical CFO who pushes back on assumptions and asks about timing and risks.
goals: Level set on current costs and explain the pass-through to customers using at least two expressions from the episode.
Argue whether to double down on the current supplier plan or change course.
Politely decline to commit on a forecast (don't bite) while still sounding credible.

useful_phrases.phrase: Let me level set for a second.
It's not that X, it's that Y.
In the short term, it's pretty limited.

shadowing.reason_ko: 'rockets and feathers' 비유를 설명하는 명쾌한 구조다. 'the dynamic everyone talks about is...'로 개념을 정의하고 대비하는 패턴을 연습하기 좋다.
'off camera', 'in reality' 같은 대비 표현과 'five alarm political fire' 같은 강한 이미지를 구어 리듬으로 말하는 연습에 좋다.
'holding out hope', 'thread the needle', 'last ditch effort' 등 정치 분석에서 쓰는 표현이 자연스러운 속도로 이어진다.

difficulty.note_ko: 빠른 구어체 속도와 정치, 에너지 시장 용어(Brent, 리파이너리, 위험 프리미엄)가 섞여 있다. 비유와 관용구가 많아 맥락 추론이 필요하지만 구조는 명확하다.

translations_sent.3-3: 이렇게 에너지 가격이 오르는 원인을 설명할 때 대통령이, 그러니까 백악관이 얼마나 뉘앙스를 담아서 이야기하고 있나요?
translations_sent.4-4: 음, 카메라가 꺼진 자리에서는 비슷한 주장을 하기도 합니다.
translations_sent.5-5: 물가상승률을 반영하면 예전만큼 나쁜 수준은 아니라는 거죠. 100달러짜리 석유가 예전에 우리가 생각하던 100달러짜리 석유는 아니라는 겁니다.
translations_sent.6-6: 하지만 현실에서는 이들에게 정치적으로 초비상 상황입니다.
translations_sent.7-7: 그리고 이번 중간선거에서 하원은 점점 더 손에 닿지 않게 됐을 뿐만 아니라, 대통령이 직접 유세를 다니는 캔자스나 사우스캐롤라이나처럼 입이 떡 벌어질 만한 곳까지 상원 판세가 넓어졌습니다.
translations_sent.8-8: 휘발유 가격은 대통령 지지율과 아주 밀접하게 연결돼 있습니다.
translations_sent.9-9: 그래서 트럼프가 집집마다 문을 두드리고 찬장이란 찬장은 다 열어보면서, 블라디미르 푸틴한테서까지 포함해 어디서든 휘발유와 경유를 한 갤런이라도 더 구하려고 하는 모습을 보셨을 겁니다.
translations_sent.10-10: 저는 데이비드 구라이고, 블룸버그 뉴스의 '더 빅 테이크'입니다.
translations_sent.11-11: 오늘은 에너지 가격이 오르고 있다는 이야기입니다.
translations_sent.13-13: 먼저 두 분 모두 이름과 성, 그리고 블룸버그에서 어떤 일을 하시는지 소개해 주시면서 시작하겠습니다.
translations_sent.19-19: 그러니까 휘발유, 경유, 항공유 같은 연료들이죠.
translations_sent.22-22: 윌, 제가 녹음에 앞서 브렌트유 가격을 확인해 봤는데요.
translations_sent.24-24: 미국에서는 휘발유 평균 가격이 갤런당, 그러니까.
translations_sent.28-28: 이 모든 걸 맥락 속에서 설명해 주시겠어요?
translations_sent.29-29: 지금 에너지 가격이 얼마나 높은 건가요?
translations_sent.31-31: 적어도 연료 쪽 에너지 가격은 우리가 본 중에서 이맘때 기준으로 가장 높은 수준입니다. 경유 6달러는 올해 전까지만 해도 전례가 없던 일이었어요.
translations_sent.32-32: 물론 과거로 돌아가서 물가상승률을 반영해 보면, 2008년이나 2022년이 더 비슷한 수준이었을 수도 있다고 말할 수는 있죠.
translations_sent.33-33: 하지만 운전자들이 주유소에서 보는 절대 가격으로는 경유가 사상 최고입니다.
translations_sent.37-37: 저희도 이 질문에 대해 확실한 답을 찾으려고 꽤 오래 매달려 온 부분입니다.
translations_sent.38-38: 백악관은 경유 가격이 오른 건 러시아 탓이라고 말해 왔죠.
translations_sent.39-39: 브렌트유 차트를 보면 2월 27일, 그리고 전쟁이 시작된 3월 첫째 주에 유가가 급등했습니다.
translations_sent.40-40: 그리고 그게 전쟁 첫 몇 달 동안 휘발유와 경유 가격이 오른 분명한 원인이었어요.
translations_sent.41-41: 호르무즈 해협을 통해 중동에서 오던 공급 손실 규모가 러시아에서 잃은 공급량보다 훨씬 큽니다.
translations_sent.42-42: 다만 우크라이나가 러시아 정유시설에 대한 드론 공격을 늘리면서 러시아에서 잃는 물량도 늘었고, 그것 역시 가격 상승에 기여했습니다.
translations_sent.43-43: 윌, 오늘 아침에 소비자물가지수 최신 수치가 나왔는데요.
translations_sent.44-44: 휘발유 가격 지수가 9월에 9% 올랐고, 이는 전체 품목의 월간 상승분 중 절반 이상을 차지했습니다. 에너지가 미국 경제 전반에서 어떤 위치에 있고, 이런 가격 상승이 경제 전체에 어느 정도 영향을 주고 있는지 설명해 주시겠어요?
translations_sent.45-45: 휘발유와 경유는 경제를 살펴보는 데 정말 좋은 두 가지 창이라고 생각해요. 휘발유는 개인 소비 품목이니까요.
translations_sent.46-46: 운전자라면, 예를 들어 미시간이나 위스콘신, 아이오와에 살면 매일 가격을 보게 되죠.
translations_sent.48-48: 매일 느끼죠. 차에 기름을 넣으면서 '탱크에 얼마를 넣어야겠네' 하고 생각하니까요.
translations_sent.49-49: 그렇긴 해도 지출 전체로 보면 휘발유 말고도 훨씬 많은 항목이 있죠.
translations_sent.50-50: 경유 가격은 다른 모든 것으로 스며듭니다.
translations_sent.51-51: 경유는 농업과 산업 말고도 주로 트럭 운송에 쓰이는 연료입니다.
translations_sent.56-56: 시간이 걸리기 때문에 경유 가격 상승의 영향이 아직 물가 지표에는 안 보일 수도 있어요.
translations_sent.57-57: 농업에서 트럭 운전사, 식료품점으로 비용이 전가되는데, 양쪽에서 쥐어짜는 셈이라 경제가 이걸 정말 체감하고 있습니다.
translations_sent.58-58: 조시, 최근 몇 주 동안 대통령과 많은 시간을 보내셨죠.
translations_sent.59-59: 공화당 후보들을 지원하는 유세 현장에도 같이 다니셨고요.
translations_sent.60-60: 이게 에너지 가격 문제로 얼마나 번졌나요?
translations_sent.61-61: 더 넓게 보면 이번 선거는 생활비 선거인데, 에너지 가격이 그 안에서 상당 부분을 차지한다고 생각해요.
translations_sent.62-62: 지난 두 번의 선거처럼 이번에도 물가 부담이 쟁점인 선거입니다.
translations_sent.63-63: 특정 인구 집단을 보여주는 여러 여론조사에서 특히 그런 모습이 보입니다.
translations_sent.64-64: 예를 들어 라틴계 유권자들은 물가 우려 때문에 2024년에 트럼프 대통령 쪽으로 크게 돌아섰어요.
translations_sent.65-65: 그런데 지금은 너무 급격하게 다시 돌아서고 있어서, 트럼프가 하원 다수당 자리를 지키려고 했던 게리맨더링 중 일부는 오히려 역효과를 낼 수도 있습니다.
translations_sent.66-66: 그래서 트럼프 입장에서는 유권자들의 우려를 가라앉히려면 무엇을 할 수 있느냐가 문제죠.
translations_sent.67-67: 그가 수표를 주겠다고 발표하는 모습도 봤는데, 특정 사람들에게 90달러 수표를 주겠다는 것도 있고, 5,000달러 수표를 약속하기도 했지만 그게 실제로 나올 거라고 믿는 사람은 많지 않죠.
translations_sent.68-68: 어쨌든 어떤 식으로든 대응하려고 하는 거죠.
translations_sent.69-69: 하지만 그는 또 도널드 트럼프라서, 어쩔 수 없이 건물 개조 같은 이런저런 다른 주제로 빠져 버립니다.
translations_sent.70-70: 그래서 이 문제에 대해 행정부가 뭘 하고 있는지 일관된 메시지가 없었어요.
translations_sent.71-71: 결국 그런 상황에 이르렀다고 할 수 있죠.
translations_sent.72-72: 지금 트럼프 행정부는 상황이 그렇게 나쁘지 않을 거라는 희망을 붙들고 있습니다.
translations_sent.74-74: 특히 상원을 마지막 보루로 삼아서 간신히 위기를 넘길 가능성도 있습니다.
translations_sent.75-75: 한 관계자는 우리 동료 캐서린 루시에게 이제 상원이 일종의 방화벽이라고 말했어요.
translations_sent.76-76: 하지만 상원 쪽 여론조사도 좋아 보이지 않아요. 텍사스, 아이오와, 오하이오, 알래스카 같은 주들이 넘어가거나 넘어갈 위험이 있다면 계산이 완전히 달라지니까요.
translations_sent.77-77: 이번은 민주당에 그리 좋은 선거 주기가 아니라고 여겨졌는데, 민주당이 상원을 뒤집을 희망이라도 갖게 됐다는 것 자체가 공화당 상황이 얼마나 나빠졌는지 보여주는 신호입니다.
translations_sent.79-79: 정치에 대한 의견을 말씀하시라고 하진 않겠습니다만, 시간 축에 대해서만 여쭤볼게요.
translations_sent.80-80: 그 기간 안에 휘발유나 디젤, 원유 가격이 눈에 띄게 내려올 가능성이나 희망이 조금이라도 있을까요?
translations_sent.82-82: 선거일 2~3주 전이라는 시간 안에는 가격이 움직일 수 있는 폭에 사실상 상한선이 있다고 봐야죠.
translations_sent.83-83: 휘발유 가격에 대해 다들 늘 얘기하는 게 '로켓과 깃털'인데, 원유가 오르면 휘발유 가격도 곧바로 로켓처럼 치솟는다는 거죠.
translations_sent.84-84: 그리고 깃털은, 내려올 때는 천천히 살살 떨어진다는 뜻이고요.
translations_sent.85-85: 지금 휘발유와 디젤 선물 시장을 보면, 당장 큰 폭의 가격 안정이 올 거라는 신호는 별로 보이지 않아요.
translations_sent.86-86: 지금 벌어지고 있는 또 다른 일은, 미국의 휘발유와 디젤 비축량이 평소 가을철에 비해 계절적으로 아주 낮은 수준이라는 거예요.
translations_sent.87-87: 그러니까 정유소에 문제가 생기거나, 송유관에 문제가 생기거나, 폭풍 때문에 멕시코만 연안에서 북동부로 연료를 못 보내게 되면 연료 가격에 상당한 영향을 줄 수밖에 없다는 뜻이죠.
translations_sent.88-88: 그러니 2~3주 안에 가격이 내려갈 수는 분명 있지만, 큰 폭으로 내려가진 않을 겁니다.
translations_sent.89-89: 조시, 대통령이 쓸 수 있는 카드가 뭐가 있는지, 그리고 최근 몇 주간 실제로 어떤 카드를 썼는지 여쭤보려던 참이었어요.
translations_sent.90-90: 그런데 당신의 찬장 비유를 빌리자면, 대통령이 그 찬장을 뒤지고 있는 셈이잖아요.
translations_sent.92-92: 유럽 국가들이 비축량 일부를 풀기로 합의했어요. 다만 얼마나, 얼마나 빨리 풀릴지는 의문이 있고요.
translations_sent.93-93: 가장 논란이 큰 건 물론 러시아가 디젤을 풀기로 한 합의죠.
translations_sent.94-94: 행정부는 그게 정확히 무슨 뜻인지 분명하게 밝히지 않았어요.
translations_sent.95-95: 초당적인 상원의원 그룹이 이에 반대하면서 위법이라고 주장하고 있습니다.
translations_sent.96-96: 2022년에 러시아 에너지를 미국으로 직접 판매하는 걸 금지하는 법이 만들어졌어요. 행정부는 그게 미국으로 들어오는 게 아니라 세계 시장에 풀려서 미국을 포함해 전반적으로 가격을 낮출 거라고 시사해 온 것 같은데, 그러면 트럼프가 푸틴에게 생명줄을 던져 준다는 비판만 더 커지겠죠.
translations_sent.97-97: 애초에 미국으로 직접 들어오지도 않는데 왜 이걸 하느냐는 거예요.
translations_sent.98-98: 이 얘기는 다른 통화에서도 나왔는데, 카니 총리실에 따르면 주말에 캐나다 총리와 한 통화에서도 나왔어요.
translations_sent.99-99: 그 통화에서도 디젤 얘기를 했다고 해요.
translations_sent.100-100: 그러니까 거의 모든 통화에서 이 얘기를 꺼내는 것 같고, 할 수 있는 건 뭐든 끌어내 보려고 닥치는 대로 전화를 돌리는 거죠.
translations_sent.101-101: 이건 행정부와 그 정책을 선거 목적에 꽤 공격적으로 쓰는 걸 주저하지 않는 그의 패턴의 일부이기도 해요.
translations_sent.102-102: 지금 그는 열어 볼 찬장 문이 점점 떨어져 가고 있다고 생각해요.
translations_sent.104-104: 그들의 관심사는 특히 캔자스 같은 주를 지키기 위해 자금을 충분히 빨리 재배치할 수 있느냐는 거예요. 캔자스는 상원 선거에서 경합주인데, 주지사는 민주당이지만 그곳이 넘어가지 않게 막아야 하니까요.
translations_sent.105-105: 그렇게 해서 51대 49나 50대 50 정도로 버티고, J.D. 밴스가 동수 때 결정표를 던질 수 있다면, 지금 눈앞에 놓인 다른 선택지보다는 그나마 나은 시나리오라고 보는 거죠.
translations_sent.106-106: 윌, 여기서 상황을 한번 정리해 달라고 부탁드릴게요.
translations_sent.108-108: 러시아가 세계 시장에 디젤 약 3,600만 배럴을 공급한다는 건데요.
translations_sent.109-109: 이게 실제로 이뤄진다면 영향은 어느 정도일까요?
translations_sent.110-110: 짧게 말하면, 적어도 단기적으로는 꽤 제한적입니다.
translations_sent.111-111: 분석가들은 트럼프가 발표하고 나중에 러시아가 확인한 디젤 물량에 꽤 실망한 상태예요.
translations_sent.112-112: 그리고 이 숫자들은 계속 바뀌는 중이라는 점도 말씀드려야겠네요.
translations_sent.113-113: 러시아 쪽에서 얼마나 풀 건지에 대해 계속 달라지는 숫자가 나오고 있거든요.
translations_sent.114-114: 그 선박들이 언제 선적할지도 알 수 없고요.
translations_sent.115-115: 앞서 말씀드렸듯이 그 물량을 미국으로 들여오는 데는 타당한 법적 장애물도 있습니다.
translations_sent.116-116: 그리고 초기 물량은, 특히 선거 전에는 디젤 가격을 움직일 만큼 충분한 규모와는 거리가 멀어요.
translations_sent.117-117: 3,600만 배럴은 한계적인 수준이고, 이게 여러 달에 걸친 물량인 데다, 겨울까지 월간 수출을 재개하는 정도를 말하는 거예요.
translations_sent.118-118: 뭐든 도움은 되죠. 지금 디젤 시장은 공급이 엄청나게 부족하니까요.
translations_sent.119-119: 브라질의 농부든 유럽에서 집을 난방하려는 사람이든, 배럴 하나라도 더 있으면 도움이 됩니다.
translations_sent.120-120: 그렇긴 하지만 러시아가 원래 어느 정도였는지를 보면, 러시아는 보통 세계 2위 디젤 수출국이거든요.
translations_sent.121-121: 이 정도로는 시장이 여전히 꽤 부족한 상태입니다.
translations_sent.122-122: 지금 겪고 있는 공급 문제를 해소하는 데 필요한 수준에는 한참 못 미친다고 말씀드리고 싶어요.
translations_sent.123-123: 이어서 조시 윙그로브, 윌 코산스키와 나눈 대화를 더 들려드리겠습니다.
translations_sent.125-125: 대통령이 디젤 수출 발표를 했고, 재무부가 러시아에 이를 허용하는 면제 조치를 내린다고 발표했어요. 사실상 유지되던 제재를 푸는 거죠.
translations_sent.126-126: 그리고 우크라이나와 러시아 사이의 이른바 에너지 휴전도 발표했고요.
translations_sent.127-127: 지난 며칠 동안 실제로 그게 무슨 의미가 있었나요, 있다면요?
translations_sent.128-128: 대통령 말로는 자신이 휴전이 존재한다고 선언했기 때문에 존재하는 휴전이라는 거예요.
translations_sent.129-129: 그러니까 결과적으로 양쪽이 합의하지 않았다는 걸, 적어도 양국 모두가 합의한 건 아니라는 걸 인정하는 셈이죠.
translations_sent.130-130: 기껏해야 아주 불안한 상태이고, 러시아에 생명줄 혹은 화해의 손길을 내민 게 아니냐는 의문에 불을 붙일 뿐 아니라, 러시아와 우크라이나 사이에 어떤 형태로든 휴전을 이끌어 내도록 미국이 우크라이나를 지원하기 위해 뭘 할 건지, 하긴 할 건지에 대한 의문도 다시 키우고 있어요.
translations_sent.132-132: 합의를 이끌어 내고 우크라이나를 지원하려는 노력에 해가 되고 그걸 약화시킨다고 생각하죠.
translations_sent.133-133: 왜냐하면 푸틴이 석유와 디젤로 이렇게 수입을 챙기면서 전쟁을 계속 밀어붙이면 어떻게 되느냐는 문제가 있으니까요.
translations_sent.134-134: 게다가 트럼프가 젤렌스키의 손발을 묶어서, 드론 공격 같은 걸로 러시아의 에너지 생산을 제한하며 반격하지 못하게 하려 하고요.
translations_sent.135-135: 그렇게 되면 안 그래도 아슬아슬하던 균형이 러시아 쪽으로 조금, 어쩌면 조금 이상으로 기울게 됩니다.
translations_sent.136-136: 그러니까 이 조치의 합법성 자체가 의심스럽다는 문제가 있고요.
translations_sent.137-137: 유럽의 많은 정상들을 포함해 동료 지도자들에게서 받은 반발도 있죠.
translations_sent.139-139: 이 부분에 대해 여쭤보고 싶었는데, 지금 정치 상황이 어떤지를 보여주는 것 같아요. 의원들이 이 일로 대통령에게 공개적으로 반대하고 있잖아요.
translations_sent.140-140: 로널드 레이건의 이름을 딴 법안까지 여기에 맞서고 있고요.
translations_sent.141-141: 이게 중간선거를 코앞에 둔 지금, 대통령이 권력을 공고히 할 수 있는 능력에 대해 무엇을 말해 주나요?
translations_sent.142-142: 네. 그리고 이건 얼마 전에 통과된 린지 그레이엄의 러시아 제재법과도 정면으로 배치되는 것 같아요.
translations_sent.143-143: 일부 공화당 의원들이 대통령에게 반대하는 목소리를 더 편하게 내는 모습이 보이는데, 경합 지역구에서 재선을 노리거나, 경합 지역이 아니길 바랐는데 판세가 10포인트 바뀌면서 갑자기 경합 지역이 됐기 때문에 그럴 수밖에 없는 거죠.
translations_sent.144-144: 아니면 대통령에게 공개적으로 경고를 보내려는 건데, 측근들로부터 나쁜 조언을 듣고 있는 건 아닌지 우려하는 거예요. 그 측근 그룹은 2025년에 대통령이 두 번째로 취임한 이후 별로 변하지 않았지만 규모는 줄어들었고요.
translations_sent.145-145: 그래서 전반적으로 공화당 내에서는 하원은 잃을 거라고 예상하고, 이제는 상원마저 뒤집힐 수 있다는 낙담이 감지된다고 봅니다.
translations_sent.146-146: 윌, 이 분야를 취재하시니 잘 아시겠지만, 그리고 대통령도 배우고 있겠지만, 글로벌 에너지 시장은 쉽게 다룰 수 없는 면이 있어요.
translations_sent.147-147: 그리고 곳곳에서 공격이 잇따르는 걸 봤죠.
translations_sent.149-149: 후티 반군이 리야드 공항과 아람코를 공격했어요.
translations_sent.151-151: 이게 전 세계 가격에 어떤 영향을 주고 있나요?
translations_sent.152-152: 네, 중동에서 추가로 분쟁이 생기면 석유의 이른바 위험 프리미엄이 올라갑니다.
translations_sent.153-153: 교전이 늘어나거나, 송유관이 공격당하거나, 선박에 대한 공격이 늘어날 거라는 기대만으로도 유가가 올라가요.
translations_sent.154-154: 그리고 지금 호르무즈 해협을 통과하는 운송 비용이 올랐어요.
translations_sent.155-155: 여전히 많은 석유가 빠져나오고 있긴 하지만, 이란의 공격 위험이 커졌거든요.
translations_sent.157-157: 그러면 결국 전 세계의 운임이 다 오르게 됩니다.
translations_sent.158-158: 그러니까 일종의 연쇄 반응이에요. 줄의 여기저기를 잡아당기면 그때마다 가격이 따라서 반응하는 걸 보게 되는 거죠.
translations_sent.159-159: 조시, 그게 중동 문제에 대한 대통령의 계산을 어떻게 바꾸고 있나요?
translations_sent.160-160: 제 말은, 정말 계속 오락가락해 왔다는 거예요.
translations_sent.164-164: 어쩌면 중간선거 때까지 기다릴 수도 있고요.
translations_sent.165-165: 사우디아라비아에서 벌어진 이번 공격과 관련해서도 트럼프 특유의, 혹은 일부러 연출한 듯한 불확실성이 나타나고 있죠.
translations_sent.166-166: 사우디가 후티 반군을 공격하는 걸 지원할 용의가 있을 수도 있다는 생각을 슬쩍 흘리기도 했고요.
translations_sent.168-168: 중동에 더 관여하거나 추가로 개입하는 문제에 대해 트럼프가 어떻게 생각하고 있다고 보세요?
translations_sent.169-169: 어제 백악관 관계자와 얘기하면서, 예컨대 사우디에 표적 정보를 제공해 주는 것이든, 더 넓게는 미국이 직접 공습을 하면서 전쟁에 참여하는 것이든, 이런 게 검토 대상에 올라 있느냐고 물었는데, 그쪽에서는 정말 답을 하려 들지 않았어요.
translations_sent.170-170: 그 관계자는 이 문제가 우선순위가 높지 않다는 취지로 말했습니다.
translations_sent.171-171: 더 큰 우려는, 이미 지지층 안에서 해외 개입에 대한 걱정이 많은 시점에 대통령이 외국 분쟁에 더 깊이 발을 들이는 모습으로 비칠 위험이 있다는 점이라고 봐요.
translations_sent.172-172: 물론 트럼프는 이란과의 이번 분쟁 과정에서 이미 여러 차례 승리를 선언했고요.
translations_sent.173-173: 그래서 지금 그쪽이 보내는 신호는 '안 한다'는 건 아니지만, 점점 더 깊이 끌려들어 가는 것에는 아주 아주 냉담하다는 겁니다.
translations_sent.174-174: 그럴 만한 이유도 분명히 있죠, 그렇지 않나요?
translations_sent.175-175: 트럼프는 해외 전쟁에 개입하지 않겠다는 메시지로 공화당을 재편한 면이 크니까요.
translations_sent.176-176: 그래서 이건 승부수를 더 던져 더 깊이 개입할지를 두고 그들이 맞닥뜨린 가장 골치 아픈 갈림길 중 하나로 남아 있다고 생각해요.
translations_sent.177-177: 그런 개입은 선거 이후에 볼 수도 있고, 아니면 사우디가 알아서 처리하도록 맡겨 두는 방법도 있겠죠. 물론 그러면 이 모든 사태의 여파를 감당하는 데 미국이 도와주지 않는다고 사우디가 불만을 품을 위험이 있고요.
translations_sent.178-178: 조시, 방금 말씀하신 것 중에 중간선거 이후에 어떻게 될지에 대해 이어서 얘기해 보고 싶어요.
translations_sent.181-181: 그때도 대통령이 에너지 가격 문제에 지금만큼, 혹은 더, 아니면 덜 관심을 쏟을까요?
translations_sent.183-183: 과거에는 궁지에 몰린 트럼프가 더 예측하기 어려운 트럼프였어요.
translations_sent.185-185: 물론 그는 선거 후에 이란에 다시 공습을 재개할 가능성도 열어 뒀어요.
translations_sent.186-186: 그 문제에 대해선 이랬다저랬다 양쪽으로 말해 왔고요.
translations_sent.187-187: 그래서 기본적으로는 뭐든 일어날 수 있다고 봐요.
translations_sent.188-188: 하지만 여기 워싱턴의 역학 관계는 달라질 겁니다.
translations_sent.189-189: 최소한 하원이 뒤집힌다면, 트럼프는 감독위원회를 비롯한 여러 위원회에서 가족 사업이나 행정부의 각종 행위에 대한 갖가지 조사를 받게 될 거예요.
translations_sent.190-190: 그러니까 목록이 끝도 없이 이어질 겁니다.
translations_sent.191-191: 게다가 이 모든 일이 2028년 대선 경쟁이 달아오르는 가운데 벌어질 거고, 그의 부통령도 이런 의혹에 점점 더 얽혀 들고 있고요.
translations_sent.192-192: 그래서 국내 정치는 그에게 꽤 빨리 복잡해질 거라고 생각해요.
translations_sent.193-193: 우리가 보기에 트럼프의 첫 번째 목표는 중간선거에서 가능한 한 최선의 결과를 얻는 겁니다.
translations_sent.194-194: 그 이후에는 많은 것이 가능하겠지만, 그는 의회 권한이 아니라 점점 행정 권한에만 의존하게 될 거예요.
translations_sent.195-195: 그게 어느 쪽으로든 나타날 수 있습니다.
translations_sent.196-196: 국내 문제에 더 집중하면서 정치적으로 벌어지는 일에 대처하거나, 아니면 이걸 자신의 업적과 관련된 사안으로 보고 직접 개입하려 들 수도 있죠.
